messages.subject: DNAcopy object
parts:
Dear Henrik,

1) Is there a way to access DNAcopy object when using CbsModel for
segmentation, assuming that DNAcopy object was created in the process
in the background?

2) in the CbsModel" step, Is there a single command that do
segmentation of several samples , each compared with the same
reference (average of normals tissues, for example)? to be more
clear, CbsModel(cesN) will generate segemetation data for each sample
against the average of cesN samples, is there a similar command to do
this with the average of a collection of normal tissues (HapMap, for
example)?

Thanks;

Han

messages.author: a5f6afcbe5b17914
messages.subject: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] DNAcopy object
parts:
On Fri, Sep 18, 2009 at 2:23 PM, han <chan...@gmail.com> wrote:
>
> Dear Henrik,
>
> 1) Is there a way to access DNAcopy object when using CbsModel  for
> segmentation, assuming that DNAcopy object was created in the process
> in the background?

If you call fit(..., .retResults=TRUE) on the segmentation model, it
will return a list of segmentation results, e.g.

cbs <- CbsModel(...);
array <- 2;
chromosome <- 4;
fit <- fit(cbs, array=array, chromosomes=chromosome, .retResults=TRUE);
fit <- fit[[1]][[chromosome]];

Then the 'fit' object is (basically) the object you get from calling
DNAcopy::segment(). There are a few extra *attributes* added. The
same is true if you use the GladModel or the HaarSegModel for
segmenation; then you get objects of that kind instead.

FYI, if it is already fitted, the segmentation will not be redone, but
the save results will be returned (same results but faster).

>
> 2) in the CbsModel" step,  Is there a single command that do
> segmentation of several samples , each compared with the same
> reference (average of normals tissues, for example)?  to be more
> clear, CbsModel(cesN) will generate segemetation data for each sample
> against the average of cesN samples, is there a similar command to do
> this with the average of a collection of normal tissues (HapMap, for
> example)?

Yes, when you go:

cbs <- CbsModel(cesN);

it is the same as doing:

ceR <- getAverageFile(cesN);
cbs <- CbsModel(cesN, ceR);

So, you can use whatever CnChipEffectFile 'ceR' (of the same chip
type) you want for you reference, e.g.

ceR <- getAverageFile(cesR);
cbs <- CbsModel(cesN, ceR);

where 'cesR' is a CnChipEffectSet of you HapMap samples.

/Henrik

>
> Thanks;
>
> Han
